title: I tried to sell a supermarket loaf of bread to people in 1795. Here's what they paid
summary: A standard sliced loaf costs about $2.30 in the US, or 19 minutes of work at the federal minimum wage. In this first episode I take it into a time machine and try to sell it three times: to a farm labourer in England in the hungry summer of 1795, where a loaf cost five hours in the field; to a builder in Rome in 301 AD, where the wheat in a loaf cost two hours but white bread was status; and to a clerk in Paris under siege in 1870, where 300 grams a day were rationed and no money bought more. The best buyer wasn't the richest. All numbers with sources in the description.
